title: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking to Elucidate the Efficacy and Potential Mechanisms of Tea Ingredients in Sepsis Treatment.
authors: Wang, Lei; Jiang, Ye; Tao, Qing; Shi, Jianfeng; Lu, Min; Yao, Xiaoming
one_liner_zh: 该文结合网络药理学与分子对接研究茶叶成分EGCG通过抑制RELA转录活性治疗脓毒症，涉及蛋白-DNA互作但非核心，方法以分子对接为主，可借鉴其对接思路但深度有限。
abstract: Sepsis, a critical health condition induced by an overactive innate immune response and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-driven host damage through apoptosis and ferroptosis, continues to pose a significant mortality risk. Despite accumulating evidence of the potential therapeutic properties of tea ingredients, their specific anti-sepsis potential remains inadequately explored. This study comprehensively investigates the targeted genes of tea ingredients, notably epigallocatechin 3-gallate (EGCG), and their correlation with sepsis signature genes. Our findings elucidate that tea ingredients, especially EGCG, exhibit substantial potential in mitigating inflammation and sepsis-induced damage. Through the inhibition of the MAPK cascade and macrophage activation and by impeding the transcriptional activity of RELA (transcription factor p65) in sepsis, EGCG demonstrates significant anti-sepsis efficacy. Molecular docking analysis further underpins this by revealing the close proximity of EGCG and (-)-catechin gallate binding sites to that of RELA on DNA. Subsequent in vitro assays illuminated EGCG's instrumental role in modulating macrophage M2 polarization, balancing M1 and M2 differentiation of bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), curtailing inflammatory factor secretion, and inhibiting ROS production. Moreover, EGCG effectively suppresses the expression of ferroptosis/apoptosis markers in LPS-induced macrophages during their early stages. Our study advances our understanding of sepsis prevention and treatment strategies, suggesting that tea ingredients such as EGCG could play a pivotal role in developing future sepsis therapies due to their protective effects.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症是一种由过度活跃的先天免疫反应及活性氧（ROS）驱动的宿主损伤（通过凋亡和铁死亡）引发的严重健康状况，持续构成显著的死亡风险。尽管茶叶成分潜在治疗特性的证据不断积累，但其特异性抗脓毒症潜力仍未得到充分探索。本研究全面调查了茶叶成分，特别是表没食子儿茶素-3-没食子酸酯（EGCG）的靶向基因，及其与脓毒症特征基因的相关性。我们的发现阐明，茶叶成分，尤其是EGCG，在减轻炎症和脓毒症诱导损伤方面展现出显著潜力。通过抑制MAPK级联反应和巨噬细胞活化，并阻碍脓毒症中RELA（转录因子p65）的转录活性，EGCG显示出显著的抗脓毒症功效。分子对接分析进一步支持这一点，揭示了EGCG和(-)-儿茶素没食子酸酯结合位点与RELA在DNA上的结合位点紧密接近。随后的体外实验阐明了EGCG在调节巨噬细胞M2极化、平衡骨髓来源巨噬细胞（BMDMs）的M1和M2分化、减少炎症因子分泌以及抑制ROS产生中的关键作用。此外，EGCG在LPS诱导的巨噬细胞早期阶段有效抑制铁死亡/凋亡标志物的表达。我们的研究推进了对脓毒症预防和治疗策略的理解，表明如EGCG等茶叶成分因其保护作用，可能在开发未来脓毒症疗法中发挥关键作用。
